faqs.a:
(a)
The municipal court judge, acting as a hearing officer, may suspend a license for
               a period of not more than six months or revoke any license granted pursuant to this
               article upon a finding of any of the following factors:
(1)
The kennel is maintained in violation of any applicable law of the state or the city;
(2)
The kennel is maintained so as to be a public nuisance; or
(3)
The kennel is maintained so as to be detrimental to the health, comfort, or safety
               of the animals therein.
(b)
A licensee shall be entitled to an administrative hearing before the municipal court
               judge if the city seeks to suspend or revoke his license based on a violation of this
               article.
(1)
Complaints about the operation of a kennel may be filed with the appropriate enforcement
               officer. When there is probable cause to believe that a licensee has violated or permitted
               a violation of this article to occur on the licensed establishment, a written complaint
               may be filed by the enforcement officer with the municipal court, setting forth the
               circumstances of the violation.
(2)
The municipal court shall provide a copy of the complaint to the licensee, together
               with notice to appear for the purpose of a hearing on a specified date to show cause
               why the licensee's license should not be suspended or revoked. The hearing shall be
               held within 30 days of the date of violation alleged in the complaint, or in a case
               where criminal prosecution of the licensee is pending, within 30 days of the date
               of entry of a plea of guilty, a no contest plea, or conviction.
(3)
The hearing referred to above shall be conducted in accordance with the procedure
               set forth in chapter 2, article V. If the municipal court judge determines that a
               violation did occur, he shall issue an order suspending or revoking the license within
               30 days after the hearing is concluded, based on the findings of fact. A copy of the
               order shall be mailed by certified mail to the licensee at the address on the license.
(4)
The order made pursuant to subsection (3) of this section shall be a final decision
               and may be appealed to the District Court pursuant to Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure
               106(a)(4). Failure of the licensee to timely appeal said order constitutes a waiver
               of any right he may otherwise have to contest the suspension or revocation of his
               license.
(c)
In the event of suspension, revocation, or cessation of business, no portion of the
               license fee shall be refunded.
(d)
When a license has been revoked, the revocation shall continue for one year, and the
               licensee shall not be issued a kennel license for one year from the date on which
               revocation became effective.
(e)
Nothing in this chapter shall prohibit the city from taking any other enforcement
               action provided for by the Code, the laws of the state, or the United States.
(Code 1981, § 6-104; Ord. No. 3496, § 2, 12-14-1998; Ord. No. 3606, § 3, 4-3-2000)
